summary: This note describes Goguryeo, a Korean kingdom that existed from 37 BCE to 668 CE across the Korean Peninsula and parts of Manchuria. At its height it controlled most of the peninsula, large parts of Manchuria, and areas of the Russian Far East and eastern Mongolia. It was one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea alongside Baekje and Silla, and it was involved in power struggles on the peninsula and in the foreign affairs of neighboring China and Japan.
one_line: Goguryeo was a Korean kingdom (37 BCE–668 CE) that rose to control much of the peninsula, Manchuria and beyond, and was one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.
key_facts: Goguryeo is also called Goryeo (고려; 高麗), which is the name the modern country of Korea derives from.
Goguryeo existed from 37 BCE to 668 CE.
Goguryeo was a Korean kingdom located in the northern and central parts of the Korean Peninsula.
Goguryeo was located in the southern and central parts of Manchuria.
At its peak of power, Goguryeo controlled most of the Korean peninsula.
At its peak of power, Goguryeo controlled large parts of Manchuria.
At its peak of power, Goguryeo controlled parts of the Russian Far East and eastern Mongolia.
Along with Baekje and Silla, Goguryeo was one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.
Goguryeo was an active participant in the power struggle for control of the Korean peninsula.
Goguryeo was associated with the foreign affairs of neighboring polities in China and Japan.
